The time-series information coefficient (IC) measures how well a signal times one asset: it is the Spearman correlation, over a window of periods, between the signal's value at the end of each period and the asset's return over the next period. The indicator owns its signal: each input updates the signal first, so the signal must not be updated elsewhere, such as by an algorithm helper that registered it. The indicator throws when it detects such an update. Because the indicator feeds its signal directly, the signal can't be built from other indicators: a CompositeIndicator is rejected, and an indicator chained with Of would get the prices instead of its source's values. The asset's price is the input's value.

To view the implementation of this indicator, see the LEAN GitHub repository.
